PARS and the catalogue label PARS-Seq refer to the same named target here. dsRNA-Seq is retained as a second target because the card title and image caption name it; its operation applicability and any alias relationship remain unresolved from the supplied paper content. This is a schematic-level extraction, not an assertion of identical complete implementations. The leftmost yellow-highlighted hairpin is an introductory method illustration without a material-transfer arrow; the material route begins at PolyA RNA. Sequencing and comparison are described in the catalogue and review but are not drawn as operations.

operations.label: RNase digestion
operations.description: RNase S1 acts on the illustrated structured polyadenylated RNA. The enzyme icon is positioned at the unpaired loop. RNA is cleaved into the pictured shorter RNA fragments with labeled 5′ P and 3′ OH ends. The enzyme is a catalyst, not a material product.
operations.mechanism: RNase S1 cleavage of RNA is illustrated at the unpaired loop. Interpreted with the catalogue nuclease-class description, this branch probes single-stranded/unpaired RNA susceptibility.
operations.information_effect: Creates RNA cleavage boundaries associated with the RNase S1 treatment, allowing structural susceptibility to be compared with the other branch. The physical carrier is the cleaved RNA and its nuclease-generated ends. Nonspecific digestion and overdigestion can distort that association; the catalogue limits the assay to in vitro applications.

Primary protocol content is required to assert a particular ligation/selective-capture mechanism or exact cleavage-site read layout. This does not block the depicted RNA-to-cDNA architecture or the reported qualitative comparison of digestion patterns.
